question: Should OpenClaw core maintain this per-handler diagnostic contract and officially catalog the performance monitor, or should the optional monitor remain external and request only narrow generic API seams?
rationale: The branch expands core diagnostic contracts and privileged internal-event access for an optional plugin, so its permanent product and ownership boundary cannot be selected safely from implementation details alone.

options.title: Narrow external plugin
options.body: Keep the monitor outside core and propose only the smallest generic SDK or diagnostic seam proven necessary.

options.title: Sponsor official plugin
options.body: Accept an official plugin after diagnostics-owner, security, contract, and live performance review.

options.title: Decline direction
options.body: Close the proposal if the observability use case does not justify new core contracts.

recommendation.title: Narrow external plugin
recommendation.body: Keep the monitor outside core and propose only the smallest generic SDK or diagnostic seam proven necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository ownership makes Peter the best available person to route or decide the core-versus-plugin product boundary.
